# KADD Layer 5 Review - Post-Implementation

**Review Date:** 2026-11-19 09:15:00 -05:00
**Scope:** `canonical/kadd/5-post-implementation/*.yaml`

## Executive Summary

The post-implementation layer remains one of the strongest knowledge-preservation surfaces in the KADD collection. The doctrines file reinforces its purpose by making learning, falsifiability, and revision central rather than incidental.

## Assessment Summary

| Dimension | Score | Rationale |
|---|---:|---| 
| Completeness | 8.9/10 | Research, lessons learned, and retrospectives are covered thoroughly. |
| Clarity | 9.2/10 | Learning output remains well structured and actionable. |
| Consistency | 9.1/10 | The new doctrine emphasis on knowledge and revision fits naturally here. |
| Coherence | 9.3/10 | The layer is strongly coherent with knowledge-first KADD philosophy. |
| Maturity | 9.0/10 | The layer demonstrates durable learning discipline. |
| Knowledge Retention | 9.4/10 | Knowledge is explicitly valued over perfect persistence of old implementations. |
| Improvement Signal | 9.2/10 | Retrospectives and research become more meaningful in a doctrine-aware framework. |
| Learning Quality | 9.3/10 | The doctrine file improves the logic behind challenge-driven learning. |

**Composite Layer Score:** 9.18/10

## Findings

### Strengths
- This layer already preserves the durable lessons of the project.
- Doctrine alignment increases the value of reflexive learning and revision.
- Research and retrospectives are explicitly connected to the project’s philosophy.

### Gaps
- Some retrospective language could cross-reference the doctrine file more directly.
- Learning records should note when assumptions were challenged or falsified.

## Recommended Actions

1. Cross-reference doctrine statements in future retrospective entries.
2. Record challenge paths and how conclusions changed over time.
3. Treat learning artifacts as durable evidence rather than narrative cleanup.
